---
title: "Text box and wrapping"
description: "Let a text clip's box fit its words, or set a width and have the words wrap, from the inspector or by dragging on the canvas."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A text clip's box decides where its lines break. By default the box fits the words, and only your own line breaks start a new line. Give it a fixed width and the words wrap to fit.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Box', 'Drag a text clip\'s left or right handle on the canvas']}
  tools="set_text"
/>

## Wrap text at a width

<Steps>

1. Select the text clip.

2. Open the **Box** section of the **Text** sub-tab.

3. Set **Mode** to **Fixed width**. The width starts at 60 % of the canvas width, which is 1,152 px on a 1920-wide canvas.

4. Type a **Width**, or drag a [side handle](#drag-the-width-on-the-canvas) on the canvas.

</Steps>

To go back, set **Mode** to **Auto-size** or choose the section's **Reset**.

## The Box section

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Mode** | **Auto-size** lays the text out without wrapping, so the box fits the words. **Fixed width** wraps the words at **Width**. | Auto-size | |
| **Width** | The width the words wrap at. It's greyed in Auto-size. | 60 % of the canvas width | 20 to 20,000 px |

A number typed outside the range is brought back to the nearest limit. Folded, the section's header reads "auto", or the width, such as "1152 px".

## Drag the width on the canvas

Drag a text clip's left or right handle in the preview to set its wrap width. If the box was on Auto-size, it becomes **Fixed width**, starting from the width it measured.

The text stays centred on the same point and grows both ways, whichever handle you drag. The drag holds the width between 4 and 20,000 px, so it can go narrower than the 20 px the **Width** field lets you type.

The other handles do something different. The corners and the top and bottom handles scale the text uniformly and leave the wrap width alone. See [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/).

## What a fixed width changes

- **The height follows the lines.** A fixed width sets only the width, and the box grows taller as the text wraps onto more lines.
- **Alignment works across the whole width.** Left, centre and right [alignment](/text-and-shapes/text-style/) line the words up against the width you set, not against the longest line.
- **A backdrop fills the whole box.** A [backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) is as wide as **Width** plus its padding, even when the words are shorter. **Width** measures the words, and the padding sits outside it.

## Good to know

- In Auto-size a long line never wraps, so it can run off the canvas. Press <kbd>⇧Return</kbd> in the [text area](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/) to start a new line yourself.
- Text is drawn at no more than 8,192 px on a side, so a box stops growing there whatever **Width** says.
- With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, **Mode**, **Width** and the side handles set the action's end, like any other text property.

## Related

- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)
- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
- [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/)
- [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/)

---
title: "Text reveals"
description: "Make a text clip type on, fade in word by word or rise in line by line, and set how long it takes to arrive and leave."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A reveal decides how a text clip's words arrive and leave. It runs from the clip's own first and last frames, so it needs no [action](/motion/actions/) and it stays in place when you move the clip.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Reveal" tools="set_text" />

## Add a reveal

<Steps>

1. Select the text clip.

2. Open the **Reveal** section of the **Text** sub-tab.

3. Choose **Typewriter**, **Word Fade** or **Line Rise** from the **Reveal** pop-up.

4. Set [**In** and **Out**](#set-how-long-it-takes) if you want something other than one second in and no exit.

</Steps>

Switching from one reveal to another keeps the times you set. Choosing **None**, or the section's **Reset**, turns the reveal off and forgets them, so the next reveal starts at 1 s in and 0 s out.

Folded, the section's header reads "off", or the reveal and its **In** time, such as "typewriter · 1.00 s".

The preview, a rendered frame and an export all work out each frame the same way, so what you see while scrubbing is what you'll export.

## The three reveals

### Typewriter

The text types on, one character at a time. Spaces and line breaks count as characters, so the typing pauses at them. On the way out it backspaces, and the end of the text goes first.

### Word Fade

The words fade in one after another. Each word's fade overlaps the next by half, so it reads as a wave across the text rather than one word at a time. On the way out they fade in the same order: the first word in is the first word out.

### Line Rise

Each line fades in as it rises into place, starting 35 % of its own height below where it ends up. The top line goes first and the others follow. On the way out each line sinks and fades, again from the top.

A line on its way up is cut off at the edge of the text box. Over a [backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) that looks like a mask, and without one the line appears to slide out of nothing.

Lines are what the box makes them. In [Auto-size](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) only your own line breaks start a new line, so a single line of text rises all at once.

## Set how long it takes

| Control | What it does | Default | Range | Quick picks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **In** | How long the arrival takes, from the clip's first frame. | 1 s | 0 to 10 s | 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 |
| **Out** | How long the departure takes, counted back from the clip's last frame. | 0 s | 0 to 10 s | 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 |

- A time of 0 means that end of the reveal doesn't happen. With **In** at 0 the text is whole on the first frame, and with **Out** at 0 it stays whole to the last.
- Both times snap to the project's frames.
- Both rows are greyed while **Reveal** is **None**.
- If **In** and **Out** add up to more than the clip's length, the two overlap. The text never shows in full, and a short clip gets a partial reveal.

A reveal has no easing control, because the motion is part of the reveal you choose.

## Word styles take over

On a caption page with a [word style](/captions/word-caption-styles/), the word style decides how the words appear. The **Reveal** section is greyed and notes "Word style wins; the reveal does not apply." The page is drawn without any reveal.

## Good to know

- **Backdrop and outline.** A backdrop stays at full strength for the whole clip, so the words type or fade onto it. An outline arrives and leaves with its letters.
- **Trimming.** **In** and **Out** are measured from the clip's edges, so a trim moves the reveal with the new edge and keeps its length.
- **Splitting.** After a [split](/editing/split/), the first piece keeps the arrival and loses the departure, and the second keeps the departure and loses the arrival. A piece left with neither has its reveal turned off.
- **Transitions.** A reveal starts on the clip's first frame, so a [transition](/motion/transitions/) into a text clip plays over the start of the reveal.
- **Nests.** Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), the text clip's own edges count, not the nest clip's. If the nest clip's edge falls part way through a reveal, the reveal is cut off there.
- **Actions.** With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, these rows set the action's end. A change of reveal switches at the action's end rather than blending. **In** and **Out** ramp like any number, which shifts the reveal's own timing while it plays, so it's usually better to set them on the clip.
- **Right-to-left text.** Typewriter can show the wrong part of a line when the text is right-to-left or mixes directions.

## Related

- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)
- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)
- [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/)
- [Entrance and exit presets](/motion/entrances-and-exits/)

---
title: "Fonts"
description: "Which fonts a text clip can use, the faces Frame Job ships with, and what happens when a project's font isn't on this Mac."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A text clip can use any font installed on your Mac, or one of the faces that come with Frame Job. Both appear in the same list, so there's nothing to set up.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Font ▸ Family" />

To choose a font, see [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/).

## Fonts the app ships with

These faces are always in the **Family** list. They need no installing, so a project that uses them draws the same on any Mac.

| Family | Weights |
| --- | --- |
| Anton | Regular |
| Bebas Neue | Regular |
| Darker Grotesque | Light to Black |
| IBM Plex Mono | Regular, Medium |
| Montserrat | ExtraBold, Black |
| Source Sans 3 | ExtraLight to Black |
| Source Serif 4 | ExtraLight to Black |

All seven are under the SIL Open Font License.

## Installed fonts

The **Family** list holds every font family on your Mac, in alphabetical order. Frame Job reads it once each time it launches, so a font you install while it's running appears after you quit and reopen it.

## When a project's font is missing

A project remembers a font by name and doesn't hold the font file. If you open it on a Mac without that font, the project still opens and the **Text** sub-tab still works.

- macOS draws the text in a stand-in font.
- **Family** shows the first family in the list, which isn't the font the project asked for.
- Picking a **Family** or **Style** replaces the missing font on that clip.

Until you pick something, the clip keeps the name of its font, so it draws correctly again once the font is installed.

:::tip
For a project you'll open on more than one Mac, use a font Frame Job ships with, or install the same font on each Mac.
:::

## Fonts in graphics

Graphics work differently. A graphic draws only with the fonts Frame Job ships with and fonts you add to the project, never with the fonts installed on your Mac. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/), including how fonts travel in a `.fjgraphic` package.

## Related

- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)
- [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/)

---
title: "Shape clips"
description: "Add a rectangle, ellipse, line or arrow at the playhead, and resize its box on the canvas."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A shape clip draws a rectangle, an ellipse, a line or an arrow over your video. Use one to frame something, point at it, or put a plate behind a title.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Add Shape in the timeline bar', 'Clip tab ▸ Shape', 'Drag a shape\'s handles on the canvas']}
  tools={['add_shape_clip', 'set_shape']}
/>

<Shot
  name="08-clip-shape.window"
  alt="The editor with an ellipse shape clip selected. In the preview a white ellipse outline has an orange frame with handles and a rotation handle, the Ellipse clip is outlined in the timeline, and the inspector shows the Shape sub-tab."
/>

## Add a shape clip

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to where the shape should start.

2. Click **Add Shape** in the timeline bar.

3. Choose **Rectangle**, **Ellipse**, **Line** or **Arrow**.

</Steps>

This button is the only way to add a shape. There's no menu item and no key.

The shape goes on the front-most track if there's room at the playhead, and otherwise on a new track in front of everything. With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, it goes in the nest. Adding it is one undo step, named after the kind, such as "Add Rectangle".

A new shape:

- lasts 5 seconds, and has no source file, so you can [trim](/editing/trim/) it to any length
- is a 320 × 120 px box with a 6 px white stroke and no fill, so it shows up over any footage
- is selected, so the **Shape** sub-tab opens on it

Everything about how it's drawn is on [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/).

## The four kinds

You can change a shape's kind at any time with [**Kind**](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/#change-the-kind).

### Rectangle

A rectangle that fills its box. A rounded rectangle is a Rectangle with a [corner radius](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/#round-a-rectangles-corners), not a separate kind.

### Ellipse

An ellipse that fills its box. Make the box square for a circle.

### Line

A straight line. A new line runs diagonally across its box, from bottom left to top right. Drag the round handle at either end to move that end. See [Lines and arrows](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/).

### Arrow

A line with an arrowhead. A new arrow runs diagonally across its box like a line, with its head at the end turned on.

## Resize with the handles

Dragging a shape's handle changes the size of its box, not a scale factor, so the stroke stays the same thickness. The box's new size shows in the **Width** and **Height** fields.

| Gesture | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Drag a corner handle | Resizes the box and keeps its aspect ratio. |
| <kbd>⇧</kbd>-drag a corner handle | Frees the aspect ratio, so width and height move independently. |
| Drag a side handle | Changes only the width or only the height. |
| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag a handle | Resizes about the centre rather than pinning the opposite handle. |

The drag holds each side of the box between 4 and 20,000 px.

<kbd>⇧</kbd> is special to shapes here. A video or picture has one uniform scale, so <kbd>⇧</kbd> changes nothing on those. For the rest of the canvas gestures, see [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/).

A box resize always changes the clip itself, even with an [action](/motion/actions/) selected. To animate a shape's size, use **Scale** in the [Transform](/canvas/transform/) section, which enlarges the whole drawing, stroke included.

## Picture sections

A shape clip has three sub-tabs: **Shape**, **Picture** and **Clip**. Its **Picture** sub-tab has these sections, in this order:

- [Transform](/canvas/transform/)
- [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/), on the top-level timeline only, so not while a nest is open
- [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/)
- [Shadow](/effects/shadow/)
- [Filters](/effects/filters/)
- [Reflection](/effects/reflection/)
- [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/)
- [Obscure](/effects/obscure/)

Crop, Corner Radius, Chroma Key and Background aren't offered, and neither is the **Color** sub-tab. To round a shape's corners, use **Corner radius** on the **Shape** sub-tab.

## With an agent

`add_shape_clip` can put a shape on any track at any time, and give it its length and look in the same step. It can also make a shape larger than the canvas, which starts scaled to fit when **Fit new clips to canvas** is on. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/).

## Related

- [Lines and arrows](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/)
- [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/)
- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)

---
title: "Shape fill, stroke and size"
description: "Change a shape's kind and box, round its corners, set its stroke and fill, and add arrowheads on the Shape sub-tab."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The **Shape** sub-tab sets what a [shape clip](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/) is and how it's painted. Where it sits, how large it's scaled and how see-through it is as a whole are on the **Picture** sub-tab, in [Transform](/canvas/transform/).

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Shape" tools="set_shape" />

<Shot
  name="08-clip-shape.inspector"
  alt="The Shape sub-tab for an ellipse. The Shape section is open with Kind set to Ellipse, Width 320 px, Height 120 px and a dimmed Corner radius at 0 px. Below it the closed sections read Stroke 6.0 px, Fill off, Gradient off and Arrowheads none."
/>

## Change the kind

**Kind** switches the shape between **Rectangle**, **Ellipse**, **Line** and **Arrow**. It changes only the kind, so everything else stays as it was.

Rows that don't apply to the new kind are greyed, not lost, so flipping the kind back finds them as you left them.

| Row | Available for |
| --- | --- |
| **Corner radius** | Rectangle |
| The **Gradient** section | Rectangle, Ellipse |
| The **Arrowheads** section | Line, Arrow |

A shape switched to **Arrow** keeps its own arrowhead setting, so a rectangle switched to Arrow has no head until you tick one. Only a shape added as an Arrow starts with a head.

## Set the size

**Width** and **Height** set the shape's box in pixels, from 1 to 20,000 px each. A new shape is 320 × 120 px. A number typed outside the range is brought back to the nearest limit.

[Dragging a handle](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/#resize-with-the-handles) on the canvas changes the same two numbers. **Scale** in [Transform](/canvas/transform/) is different: it enlarges the finished drawing, stroke included.

## Round a rectangle's corners

**Corner radius** rounds a rectangle's corners, from 0 to 2,000 px, with quick picks at 0, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64. The default is 0. It's greyed for other kinds.

A radius can't go past half the box's shorter side. At that point the short ends are fully round, and a larger number looks the same.

The **Shape** section's **Reset** puts the corner radius back to 0, and leaves the kind and the box alone.

## Draw an outline

The **Stroke** section draws an outline around the shape. A new shape has one.

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Stroke** | Turns the outline on or off. | On | |
| **Width** | How thick it is. Quick picks 1, 2, 4, 6, 12 and 24. | 6 px | 0.5 to 200 px |
| **Color** | Its colour. | White | |

**Width** and **Color** are greyed while the stroke is off. Turning the stroke off forgets its width and colour, so turning it on again gives 6 px white. **Reset** also goes back to 6 px white rather than turning the stroke off.

On a rectangle or ellipse the stroke sits inside the box, so a thicker stroke doesn't make the shape bigger.

Folded, the section's header reads the width, such as "6.0 px", or "off".

## Fill the shape

The **Fill** section paints the inside of a rectangle or ellipse with a flat colour. A new shape has no fill.

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Fill** | Turns the fill on or off. | Off | |
| **Color** | The fill's colour. | White, once turned on | |
| **Opacity** | How solid the fill is. Quick picks 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100. | 100 % | 0 to 100 % |

**Color** and **Opacity** are greyed while the fill is off. Turning the fill off forgets its colour, so turning it on again gives opaque white. **Reset** turns the fill off.

**Opacity** belongs to the fill alone, so it doesn't fade the stroke. To fade the whole shape, use **Opacity** in [Transform](/canvas/transform/).

Folded, the section's header reads the fill's opacity, such as "100%", or "off".

For a colour ramp in place of a flat colour, see [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/). A gradient covers the fill while it's on, and turning it off brings the fill back.

## Add arrowheads

The **Arrowheads** section has two separate boxes, **Arrowhead at start** and **Arrowhead at end**. They're available for lines and arrows, and greyed for rectangles and ellipses.

:::note
Arrowheads are drawn only when **Kind** is **Arrow**. On a Line you can tick the boxes and they're kept, but no head appears until you switch the kind to Arrow.
:::

Folded, the section's header reads "both", "start", "end" or "none". See [Lines and arrows](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/) for moving the ends.

A line or arrow is drawn with its stroke, so a Line with **Stroke** off shows nothing. **Fill** paints nothing on a line or arrow, although its rows stay available. The one exception is an Arrow with **Stroke** off, whose heads take the fill colour.

## Why shape colours don't animate

An [action](/motion/actions/) can't change a shape's kind, stroke, fill, gradient or arrowheads. These rows always change the clip itself, even while an action is selected, and they're marked ⊘ to show it.

A shape's position, scale and opacity animate like any clip's. To move or fade a shape, select an action and use the [Transform](/canvas/transform/) rows on the **Picture** sub-tab. See [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).

## With an agent

`set_shape` changes any of these settings in one call and leaves the rest as they are, including a line's two ends. A shape's position and scale aren't part of it: those go through `set_video`. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Good to know

Shapes are drawn at no more than 8,192 px on a side, however large the box is.

## Related

- [Shape clips](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/)
- [Lines and arrows](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/)
- [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/)
- [Transform](/canvas/transform/)
